speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how many workers over the age of 63 have lost their jobs in retrenchment exercises in the last five years; and (b) whether a higher proportion of workers in this age group have lost their jobs as compared to other age groups.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the rationale under the Tripartite Guidelines for Fair Employment Practices for workers who are losing their entitlement to retrenchment benefits to be entitled only to Employment Assistance Payments upon reaching the age of 63; and (b) whether the guidelines can be amended to reduce a "cliff effect" in the drop in retrenchment entitlement for long-serving workers upon turning 63.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: First, the data shows that workers who are past the retirement age are not disproportionately affected by retrenchment, compared to other age groups.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Retirement and Re-employment Act requires employers to offer re-employment to employees above the prevailing retirement age and below the prevailing re-employment age, or else employers will need to pay eligible employees the Employment Assistance Payment, or EAP.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The recommended EAP amount in the Tripartite Guidelines on Re-employment of Older Employees is carefully calibrated.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The EAP should not be so low that it provides employers an easy alternative to offering their employees re-employment.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: However, if the EAP is too high, it may deter employers from hiring or retaining senior workers nearing retirement age in the first place.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In some cases, there is an agreement between the union and the employer to scale down the quantum of retrenchment benefits payable as the worker nears the statutory retirement age.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Any real or perceived "cliff effect" between retrenchment benefits and EAP is dependent on the quantum of retrenchment benefits stipulated in the individual's employment contract or the collective agreement.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: The Ministry of Manpower (MOM) will continue to work closely with the tripartite partners to review our retirement and re-employment policies, to ensure they remain relevant and foster progressive workplaces that enable our senior workers to continue working if they wish to.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, what I was informed is that for many senior workers who are above the age of 63, their EAP benefits are no longer tied to their years in service.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, what this means is, in substance, up to the age of 63, they are very expensive to lay off if they have been working for a long time.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: But after the age of 63, the EAP payments are no longer based on years in service.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, someone who was very expensive to lay off or retrench at the age of 63, suddenly becomes very cheap to lay off.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And because senior workers also have the greatest difficulty getting re-employment, I think it is important for them to be protected.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: My first clarification is: the figure that was given for workers over 63, that is, only 3.8 per 1,000 were retrenched, does this also take into account workers who may have been retired and not re-employed?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: Because I understand that is the mechanism that is sometimes used.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: So, the worker is not actually re-employed and given early retirement.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: The second is, I think the Senior Minister of State has mentioned that the EAP is carefully calibrated and open to negotiation.

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: I have two related clarifications on this: first, in relation to employees who have the benefit of collective agreements, how many of these collective agreements tie the EAP payments to years in service?

speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
text: And second, for employees without collective agreements, how many of them are eligible for retrenchment payments?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: I just want to correct the statement that was made.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Therefore, it is not something that is tied to years of service, but it is meant to be something that tides them over a couple of months, for example, till the person can find a new job.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Because if the EAP amount is too high, employers may then be concerned with excessive cost burden of the re-employment obligation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And then, they will be less willing to retain a senior worker up to the retirement age.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In other words, they may choose to then retrench the worker before the retirement age.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: This would then be detrimental to senior workers who are close to retirement age.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: We want to avoid disincentivising also senior workers from searching for alternative employment if they are not successfully re-employed.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: It really is about getting enough for them to tide them over a period, but not to be such a windfall that there is no more incentive to look for other employment opportunities that come along the way.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And we also should not be creating a perverse incentive to employers to not retain workers close to the retirement age.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But this is not mandated by law and this is something that companies and their employees will have to come to an agreement on.
